sampling: one discarded warm-up, then measured repetitions (repeat 200 GPU default, 120 GPU large, 3 CPU); reported value is the median.
timing_scope: kernel enqueue + device synchronization only (host/device copies, references, allocation, verification excluded)

tolerance.rationale: HeCBench Verify uses 0.05. The escape-time map is chaotic on the parabolic boundary; a float/double last-bit difference moves isolated boundary pixels. Measured float/double divergence worst case 0.0075, about 7x below the bound. Exact float comparison, finite/range guards and an exact deep-interior spot check pass independently.

environment.cpu: rosi_v100 host 48-core EPYC, GCC 13.2, OMP_NUM_THREADS=48, alpaka backend CpuOmpBlocks
environment.gpu: rosi_v100: NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB, sm_70, CUDA 12.6, g++ 13.2, alpaka backend GpuCuda

reference_caveats: The HeCBench OpenMP reference is an OpenMP-offload program whose host fallback only uses threads when a target is present; its host number is indicative, not a strict like-for-like CPU ratio.
The rosi_v100 node is shared (load average 30-50), so CPU timings vary run to run; GPU medians use a long warm-up and repeat>=120 to avoid the V100 clock ramp.

verification.faithful_float_reference: GPU boundary-pixel FMA differences only (4702/1048576), CPU 0 mismatches; both within tolerance
verification.finite_and_range_guards: PASSED (device image poisoned with NaN before the kernel)
